newsitem.title: USA: U.S. files charges on illegally smuggled freon gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. files charges on illegally smuggled freon gas.

text.p: The Clinton administration said on Thursday criminal charges have been filed in four states as part of a crackdown against smugglers who bring freon gas into the United States.

Justice Department, Environmental Protection Agency and Customs Service officials said the latest charges stemmed from a 1994 initiative aimed at stopping imports of the banned chemical, also known as chlorofluorocarbon or CFC-12.

They told a news conference charges have been filed in the past several days in San Diego, Los Angeles, Houston, Miami and Savannah, Georgia, against 12 individuals. The officials said 18 convictions already have been obtained.
Attorney General Janet Reno said the problem of illegally imported freon gas, which was banned in the United States a year ago to protect the ozone layer, has become more severe.
"To CFC smugglers, we say: 'We will find you, we will shut down this black market and we will not let you endanger our ecosystem ... for a few dollars,'" she said.
Customs Commissioner George Weise said the freon was being smuggled into the United States across both borders and by ship. Much of it comes from Russia, India or China, he said.
Weise said some smugglers were involved in Russian organised crime and that the problem had shifted from Miami to the Southwest U.S. border, just as with drug smuggling.
Officials said they have seized about 1.5 million pounds (680,400 kg) of freon gas, worth an estimated $18 million, in the crackdown.
